**Self-disclosure and social media: motivations, mechanisms and psychological well-being** (URL: [https://socialmedialab.sites.stanford.edu/sites/g/files/sbiybj22976/files/media/file/luo-copsych-self-disclosure.pdf](https://socialmedialab.sites.stanford.edu/sites/g/files/sbiybj22976/files/media/file/luo-copsych-self-disclosure.pdf))   
*(Published February 2020\)*

* Self-disclosure: any message about oneself that an individual communicates w/ other people   
    * Varies across multiple dimensions that generally fall into either quantity (i.e., frequency, duration, depth) or quality (i.e., accuracy, intention, and valence)  
* Psychological well-being: a construct involving both psychological adjustment and negative maladjustment  
* Internet-enhanced self-disclosure (IESD) hypothesis \-\> argues that online self-disclosure enhances relationship quality to a greater degree than face-to-face disclosures. This relational effect in turn enhances the impact that self-disclosure has on well-being in computer-mediated communication relative to face-to-face  
* Competing hypotheses on the antecedents of self-disclosure in social media:  
    * *Social compensation hypothesis (‘poor-get-richer’)*  
        * Expects lonely/socially anxious people to use online communication more frequently  
    * *Enhancement hypothesis (‘rich-get-richer’)*  
        * Predicts that socially competent individuals will consider social media as additional venues for social interactions  
* Four prominent mechanisms that may account for the effects of self-disclosure on well-being:  
    * Perceived connectedness   
    * Social support  
    * Capitalization process  
    * Psychological authenticity

![][image1]

* Perceived connectedness \-\> the feeling of relatedness w/ one another in their lives  
    * Since social media allow for public disclosure, and disclosure often predicts interpersonal intimacy in dyadic interaction, a more general feeling of connection is expected from disclosing in public, which improves well-being  
    * Research has shown that posting status updates about personal daily experience can increase connectedness, which can reduce loneliness  
* Social support \-\> social benefits (e.g., emotional, informational, and instrumental help) that people perceive, express, & gain from human interactions  
    * Involves both perceived (i.e., the general impression) and enacted social support (i.e., the specific supportive behaviors)  
    * Can have direct positive impact on psychological well-being as it ‘provides positive affect, a sense of predictability & stability in one’s life situation, & a recognition of self-worth’)  
    * Disclosers become more aware of other’s attentiveness to their needs, and thus may perceive higher levels of social support via posting then looking at responses (one-click communication like comments, likes, etc.)  
* Capitalization and authenticity \-\> expressing personal thoughts & emotions have additional effects on psychological well-being because it increases the salience & significance of the events, and allows people to rearrange their memories about the events, and allows people to rearrange their memories about the events during the course of expression (in other words, people feel more positive sharing positive emotional disclosure and more negative sharing negative disclosure)  
    * ‘Positivity norm’ of internet culture \-\> positive disclosure often occurs more frequently and predicts positive feedback and more social support, which in turn can increase feelings of connectedness  
    * Negative disclosure (via status updates) may discourage others from providing public responses  
    * While receiving feedback may enhance self-esteem, a lack of feedback may lead to sense of ostracism (detrimental to overall well-being)   
    * Social media may also push selective self-presentation, and thus allow for self-expression that may be inconsistent w/ people’s true selves  
        * Recent evidence has shown that accurate & authentic self-disclosure can benefit general well-being & improve self-esteem among mindful people  
        * Inaccurate & inauthentic self-disclosure may make people feel less socially connected & more stressed  
* Interpersonal motives: relational development  
    * Disclosure driven by relational development seeks to increase relational intimacy and closeness w/ another person  
        * This motive is associated w/ more frequent self-disclosure in social media   
        * Predicts more intentional, positive, & honest disclosure  
    * People w/ low self-esteem disclosed a wider variety of topics on Facebook than those w/ high self-esteem  
    * Lonely people were more likely to disclose on social media due to their stronger motives for social compensation & social networking  
* Intrapersonal motives: self-expression  
    * Seeks to ‘express feelings & thoughts and release pent-up feelings’  
    * Traditional research argues that people w/ psychological distress are drawn to self-expression because they can buffer stress by releasing the ‘fever’ of those pent-up feelings through self-expression  
        * Study found that higher level of stress triggered greater amounts of self-disclosure in social media   
            * Possible explanation: people low in self-esteem may perceive social media as a safer medium for self-expression & a more appealing place for social compensation (more attention & support from others)  
    * Self-expression motives are likely to encourage negative social sharing   
        * This negativity effect appears to take place on image-based social media platforms, such as Instagram, as well  
            * Recent study showed that depressed individuals were more likely to post darker, bluer, and  greyer images than healthy people  
* **It may be difficult for distressed individuals to benefit from self-disclosure on social media**  
    * **They may be less honest in their disclosures online (“false self” persona online may make people feel even more depressed & less connected)**  
* **Although negative disclosure may gratify the intrapersonal needs for emotional venting and self-expression, it may impair relational goals**  
    * Study showed that although depressed participants can actually obtain more Facebook social support from their negative sharing, they failed to perceive the wealth of support compared to healthier disclosers  
* **There may be benefits, however:**  
    * **Negative disclosure via private messaging may be more likely to receive responses than public status updates**  
    * **Online forums (e.g., Reddit) allow for people to use anonymous accounts \-\> anonymity can reduce senders’ perceived vulnerability of stigmatized content which may encourage more honest disclosure**  
        * For example, anonymous posts on Reddit have been shown to involve more negative discourse on mental health and to receive more emotional & instrumental support than non-anonymous posts
